corrections.finding: Dropped 'mostly' before 8 to 10; 'vertebrate' is not in the source; a 'passing T cell' is cytotoxic and must match a foreign piece, and the source says it recognizes and kills; 'sharing its own interior's parity across' and 'its sharing's is-not observing' are unclear and have no source.
corrections.fixed_text: Nearly each cell with a nucleus shows on its surface short pieces, mostly 8 to 10 amino acids long, of the proteins it is making within; a passing cytotoxic T cell whose receptor matches a piece foreign to the body, a virus's for one, recognizes and kills that cell, and a cell showing too little of these pieces meets a natural killer cell's attack.

corrections.finding: Claim stronger than source: the source says inflammation opens chromatin sites and some stay open, and the memory (not the sites) lasted up to six months; 'sooner' changes 'more effectively'; 'a field files outside its immune system' has no source, and the article does not say whether immune cells were required.
corrections.fixed_text: Skin epithelial stem cells keep a memory of an earlier inflammation, up to six months in mice: the inflammation opens sites in their chromatin and some stay open, and a later wound in that skin closes more than twice as fast, the stem cells moving into it more effectively: a memory of inflammation in skin stem cells.

corrections.finding: 'carry' is a dissolved word (source: express); 'membrane contact' is vague (source: direct contact seen by electron microscopy); 'third-degree' uses a dissolved word; 'the myeloid cells removing' drops 'macrophages and other'; 'their connexin-43 removing' is unclear; 'heart's own beating' is wider than AV conduction.
corrections.fixed_text: Macrophages in the heart's atrioventricular node express connexin-43 and touch heart muscle cells directly, as electron microscopy shows; deleting their connexin-43 impairs the node's conduction, and depleting macrophages and other myeloid cells brings a first-degree block within 24 hours, progressing to complete heart block, the last of three degrees: cells a field calls immune take part in the heart's own conduction.

corrections.finding: Prediction made into fact: the theory predicts tolerance or response, it does not say they happen; 'fast-growing cells' changes the source's fast-growing tumour; 'gut's long-dwelling microbes' changes 'microbiota acquired early and persisting' (gut not in source); the motifs engaging immune receptors are dropped; last clause 'a changing of a not-changing, a parity of now beside a prior' is unclear.
corrections.fixed_text: One theory, discontinuity theory, reads immunity this way: an immune response comes with the speed of change in the molecular motifs a tissue shows to immune receptors, not with a thing's origin; a persistent or slowly appearing motif is predicted to meet tolerance, microbes that arrive early and persist among them, and a sudden change, even in a body's own fast-growing tumour, is predicted to meet a response.

corrections.finding: Claims stronger than the observings: 'each cell' (source: nearly all nucleated cells); 'skin stem cells keep an inflammation's opening' (some sites stay open); 'heart macrophages carry the beat' (source: needed for AV conduction); one theory's reading stated flat as 'a body responds to the speed of change' and then as the conclusion 'so immunity is...' though item 4 calls it one field's reading.
corrections.fixed_text: An immune system of fighter cells apart from other cells is a field's explaining: nearly each cell with a nucleus shows pieces of its own interior on its surface, skin stem cells keep a memory of an earlier inflammation, heart macrophages take part in the node's conduction, and one theory reads a body's response by the speed of change; by that reading, immunity is a body's same-existing-society observing change beside its prior with each of its selves, a defending and a fighting being a field's words.

corrections.fixed_text: Within one body a same-existing-society discovers: nearly each cell with a nucleus shows pieces of its own making on its surface, a passing cytotoxic T cell whose receptor matches a foreign piece recognizes and kills that cell, and among B cells competing in a germinal centre, higher-affinity antibodies arise over time, in no cell alone.
